title: The Trinity
subtitle: One God: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and what each does toward the others, from the first page of Scripture to the last
summary: The word "Trinity" is not in the Bible, but what it names is there on almost every page. Scripture says plainly that God is one: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One." It also calls three persons God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. They are not three names for one person, because they speak to one another, send one another, love and glorify one another; and they are not three gods, because God is one. Christians were using the word "Trinity" by about AD 200 to hold those truths together, and the Nicene Creed (325, enlarged in 381) put them in the words most churches still confess. This study gathers the passages behind it. The triangle chart draws them the way medieval Christians drew the Shield of the Trinity: the three persons at the corners, God at the center, a spoke from each corner for the passages that call that person God, and on each side a line each way for what one does toward the other: the Father sends the Son, the Son prays to the Father, the Son sends the Spirit, the Spirit glorifies the Son. The passages where all three act at once, from Jesus's baptism to the blessing that ends 2 Corinthians, ring the center.

facets.title: Who relates to whom
facets.note: Where each passage sits on the triangle. One passage can sit in several places.

values.title: All three together
values.note: Passages where the Father, the Son and the Spirit all act at once.

values.title: The Spirit is God, and a person
values.note: The Spirit speaks, wills, teaches, can be lied to and grieved: not a force but a person.

facets.title: What they do
facets.note: The verbs of the relationships. A passage can carry several.

corners.title: The Father
corners.note: The first person of the Trinity, to whom Jesus prayed as “Abba.”

corners.title: The Son
corners.note: The Word made flesh: Jesus Christ.

corners.title: The Holy Spirit
corners.note: The Spirit of God and the Spirit of Christ, sent to live in God's people.

center.title: One God
center.note: “The LORD our God, the LORD is One.”

views.title: How they relate
views.note: One God, each person God, each pair of persons, and all three together.

groups.title: God is one
groups.note: The ground floor of the doctrine: there is one God and no other. The New Testament never gives this up; it places Jesus inside it.

refs.label: “The LORD our God, the LORD is One”
refs.note: The Shema, Israel's daily confession.

links.label: Mark 12:28–30
links.topic: Jesus calls it the first commandment

refs.label: “I am the LORD, and there is no other”
refs.note: “There is no God but Me.”

refs.label: “Let Us make man in Our image”
refs.note: God speaks in the plural, then creates man “in His own image” in the singular. Early Christians heard in the “Us” a first hint of more than one person in the one God.

refs.label: Jesus: “the Lord is One”
refs.note: Asked for the greatest commandment, Jesus answers with the Shema.

refs.label: One God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ
refs.note: “There is no God but one.” Then Paul splits the Shema's two words between them: “one God, the Father, from whom all things came … one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came.”

refs.label: One God, and one mediator
refs.note: “There is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

groups.title: The Father is God
groups.note: Rarely in doubt: Jesus prays to him and teaches us to. Scripture calls him the Father of Jesus, of Israel, and of all who believe.

refs.label: “Do we not all have one Father?”
refs.note: “Did not one God create us?” Already in the prophets God is Father to his people.

refs.label: “Our Father in heaven”
refs.note: Jesus teaches his disciples to pray to his Father as their own.

refs.label: “On Him God the Father has placed His seal”
refs.note: The Father sets his seal of approval on the Son of Man.

refs.label: “My Father and your Father, My God and your God”
refs.note: Risen, Jesus calls the disciples his brothers and shares his Father with them.

refs.label: “The Father of the heavenly lights”
refs.note: Every good and perfect gift comes down from him, “with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.”

groups.title: The Son is God
groups.note: The Son is called God, worshiped, and credited with creating the world, yet he is not the Father: he is with God, at the Father's side, sent by him.

refs.label: “Mighty God”
refs.note: The child born to us will be called “Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.”

links.label: Luke 1:32–33
links.topic: The throne of his father David

refs.label: “The Word was with God, and the Word was God”
refs.note: With God, so distinct from the Father; God, so not less than him. “Through Him all things were made.”

refs.label: “The Word became flesh”
refs.note: “We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father.”

refs.label: “The one and only Son, who is Himself God”
refs.note: “No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father's side, has made Him known.”

refs.label: “Making Himself equal with God”
refs.note: His opponents understood what calling God “His own Father” meant.

refs.label: “Before Abraham was born, I am!”
refs.note: Echoing the name God gave Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:14). His hearers picked up stones.

refs.label: “I and the Father are one”
refs.note: One, yet “I and the Father,” two. They answer: “You, who are a man, make Yourself out to be God.”

refs.label: “My Lord and my God!”
refs.note: Thomas, touching the wounds; Jesus accepts the worship.

refs.label: In the form of God, obedient to death
refs.note: “Existing in the form of God,” he emptied himself and “became obedient to death.” So the Father exalted him, and every tongue confesses him Lord “to the glory of God the Father.”

refs.label: “The image of the invisible God”
refs.note: “All things were created through Him and for Him … For God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him.”

refs.label: “All the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form”
“Christ, who is God over all”
refs.note: “Forever worthy of praise! Amen.”

refs.label: “Our great God and Savior Jesus Christ”
“The exact representation of His nature”
refs.note: God has spoken by his Son, “through whom He made the universe”; the Son is “the radiance of God's glory.”

refs.label: “Your throne, O God, endures forever”
refs.note: The Father speaks to the Son and calls him God, then says “God, Your God, has anointed You.”

groups.title: The Holy Spirit is God, and a person
groups.note: The Spirit is everywhere God is, knows what only God knows, and is called God. He also speaks, decides, teaches, and can be lied to and grieved: he, not it.

refs.label: “Where can I go to escape Your Spirit?”
refs.note: The Spirit is as present everywhere as God himself.

refs.label: “They rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Even here the Spirit is someone who can be grieved. The passage names the LORD, “the Angel of His Presence,” and “His Holy Spirit” together.

links.label: Ephesians 4:30
links.topic: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God”

refs.label: Blasphemy against the Spirit
refs.note: Jesus speaks of sinning against the Spirit as worse than speaking against the Son of Man.

refs.label: “You have not lied to men, but to God!”
refs.note: Peter says Ananias lied “to the Holy Spirit,” then that he lied to God.

refs.label: “The Holy Spirit said, ‘Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul’”
refs.note: The Spirit speaks, and calls people to himself.

refs.label: The Spirit searches the deep things of God
refs.note: “No one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.” We have received “the Spirit who is from God.”

refs.label: “You yourselves are God's temple”
refs.note: The temple is God's because “God's Spirit dwells in you.”

refs.label: “As He determines”
refs.note: The Spirit gives each believer gifts by his own will.

refs.label: “Now the Lord is the Spirit”
refs.note: “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”

refs.label: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God”
refs.note: The seal on every believer until the day of redemption.

groups.title: The Father and the Son
groups.note: The Father loves, sends, gives, shows and glorifies; the Son obeys, reveals, prays and glorifies in return. The richest side of the triangle, and most of it in Jesus's own words.

refs.label: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father”
refs.note: The LORD speaks to his anointed king. The apostles heard the Father speaking to Jesus.

refs.label: “The LORD said to my Lord”
refs.note: Jesus asked how David, speaking “in the Spirit,” could call his own descendant Lord: the LORD, David's Lord, and the Spirit in one verse.

links.label: Matthew 22:41–45
links.topic: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is

refs.label: One like a Son of Man before the Ancient of Days
refs.note: He is given dominion, glory and a kingdom that will never be destroyed. At his trial Jesus took this vision for himself.

refs.label: “God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son”
refs.note: The Father's love for the world is measured by what the Son is to him.

refs.label: “The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does”
refs.note: The Son does only what he sees the Father doing; the Father has given him all judgment and “granted the Son to have life in Himself,” so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.

refs.label: “Not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me”
“Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father”
refs.note: “No one comes to the Father except through Me … I am in the Father and the Father is in Me.”

refs.label: “The Father is greater than I”
refs.note: Christians have read this of the Son as sent and made man, since the same Gospel opens by calling him God (1:1), and near its end Thomas calls him “My Lord and my God” (20:28).

refs.label: “I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me … I love the Father”
refs.note: The only place Jesus says in so many words that he loves the Father.

refs.label: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son”
refs.note: Jesus prays: “that Your Son may glorify You … glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Eternal life is to know “the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.”

refs.label: “As You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You”
refs.note: He prays that his people may be one as they are one, and share the love the Father had for him “before the foundation of the world.”

refs.label: “This is My beloved Son … Listen to Him!”
refs.note: The Father's voice again, on the mountain of transfiguration.

refs.label: “Not as I will, but as You will”
refs.note: In Gethsemane the Son asks, and yields.

refs.label: “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit”
refs.note: His last words from the cross are a prayer to the Father.

refs.label: “He who did not spare His own Son”
refs.note: “But gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?”

refs.label: “An advocate before the Father”
refs.note: The risen Son speaks to the Father for us. “Advocate” is the word Jesus used when he promised the Spirit as “another Advocate.”

refs.label: “God sent His one and only Son into the world”
refs.note: “Not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.”

refs.label: He hands over the kingdom to God the Father
refs.note: At the end the Son hands the kingdom to the Father, “so that God may be all in all.”

groups.title: The Son and the Spirit
groups.note: The Spirit conceives, anoints, leads, empowers and raises the Son; the Son pours out the Spirit; the Spirit glorifies the Son.

refs.label: The Spirit descends and rests on Him
refs.note: John the Baptist is told that the one on whom the Spirit rests “is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: Full of the Spirit, led by the Spirit
refs.note: Into the wilderness to be tempted, then back to Galilee “in the power of the Spirit.”

refs.label: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me”
refs.note: In Nazareth Jesus reads Isaiah 61 and says “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

refs.label: “If I drive out demons by the Spirit of God”
refs.note: “Then the kingdom of God has come upon you.” The Son's works are done in the Spirit's power.

refs.label: Streams of living water
refs.note: “He was speaking about the Spirit … the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.”

refs.label: “If I go, I will send Him to you”
refs.note: The Son's going away is for their good: then he sends the Advocate, who convicts the world.

refs.label: “Through the Spirit of holiness … declared with power to be the Son of God”
refs.note: By his resurrection from the dead.

refs.label: “Put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit”
“No one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except by the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Every true confession of the Son is the Spirit's work.

groups.title: The Father and the Spirit
groups.note: The Spirit is the Father's own Spirit, sent and given by him, who searches the Father's mind and prays according to his will.

refs.label: “The Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters”
refs.note: At creation, before God speaks.

refs.label: “When You send Your Spirit, they are created”
“I will put My Spirit within you”
refs.note: A new heart, and God's own Spirit moving his people to walk in his ways.

refs.label: “I will pour out My Spirit on all people”

links.label: Acts 2:16–18
links.topic: Peter: this is what Joel spoke of

refs.label: “How much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: “To those who ask Him!”

refs.label: The Spirit intercedes “according to the will of God”
refs.note: He prays for us “with groans too deep for words,” and the Father who searches hearts “knows the mind of the Spirit.”

groups.title: All three together
groups.note: The passages where the Father, the Son and the Spirit act at once: at the Son's conception and baptism, in his last teaching, at Pentecost, and in every part of a Christian's life.

refs.label: “Holy, holy, holy”: whose glory, and whose voice?
refs.note: Isaiah sees the Lord, the seraphim cry “holy” three times, and God asks “Who will go for Us?” John says Isaiah saw Jesus' glory; Paul says the Holy Spirit spoke these words.

links.label: Acts 28:25–26
links.topic: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke”

refs.label: “The Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit”
refs.note: A speaker sent by the Lord GOD, with his Spirit.

refs.label: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me”
refs.note: The Spirit, the LORD who anoints, and the one anointed: the scroll Jesus read in Nazareth.

refs.label: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you”
refs.note: “And the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God.”

refs.label: The baptism of Jesus
refs.note: The Son comes up out of the water, the Spirit descends like a dove and rests on him, and the Father's voice says “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”

refs.label: “God gives the Spirit without limit”
refs.note: The one God sent speaks God's words, “for God gives the Spirit without limit. The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.”

refs.label: “Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Rejoicing in the Spirit, the Son praises the Father: “All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son.”

refs.label: “God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power”
refs.note: Peter's summary of Jesus's whole ministry, “because God was with Him.”

refs.label: “I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate”
refs.note: The Son asks, the Father gives, the Spirit comes “in My name” to teach. “My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.”

refs.label: “The Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father”
refs.note: The Son sends the Spirit “from the Father,” and the Spirit testifies about the Son. The Nicene Creed takes “proceeds from the Father” from this verse; Western churches later added “and the Son,” a difference still discussed between East and West.

refs.label: “He will glorify Me”
refs.note: The Spirit takes what is the Son's and makes it known; “Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine.”

refs.label: “As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you”
refs.note: Then he breathed on them: “Receive the Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: One name, three persons. The Didache, one of the earliest Christian writings outside the Bible, baptizes in the same words.

refs.label: “Wait for the gift the Father promised”
refs.note: The Son tells them to wait for the Father's promise: baptism with the Holy Spirit.

refs.label: Raised, exalted, and pouring out the Spirit
refs.note: “God has raised this Jesus to life … He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.” Pentecost is all three at once.

refs.label: “Through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God”
refs.note: The cross itself: the Son offers himself to the Father through the Spirit.

refs.label: The Spirit of God, the Spirit of Christ
refs.note: One Spirit called by both names; the Spirit of him who raised Jesus will give life to our mortal bodies.

refs.label: “By whom we cry, ‘Abba! Father!’”
refs.note: The Spirit of adoption makes us God's children and co-heirs with Christ.

refs.label: God sent His Son, and the Spirit of His Son
refs.note: “God sent His Son … God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, ‘Abba, Father!’”

refs.label: The same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God
refs.note: Gifts, ministries and ways of working, each traced to one of the three.

refs.label: The grace, the love, and the fellowship
refs.note: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.”

refs.label: Chosen, redeemed, sealed
refs.note: The Father chose us “before the foundation of the world,” in the Son “we have redemption through His blood,” and we were “sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “Access to the Father by one Spirit”
refs.note: “Through Him,” the Son. Christian prayer runs through all three.

refs.label: One Spirit, one Lord, one God and Father of all
Loved by the Lord, chosen by God, sanctified by the Spirit
“Renewal by the Holy Spirit … poured out on us through Jesus Christ”
refs.note: God our Savior saved us, the Spirit renews us, and the Son is the one through whom the Spirit is poured out.

refs.label: Chosen by the Father, sanctified by the Spirit, for Jesus Christ
refs.note: “According to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ.”

refs.label: “He has given us of His Spirit”
refs.note: “And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent His Son to be the Savior of the world.”

refs.label: Praying in the Spirit, kept in God's love, awaiting Christ's mercy

views.title: Through the story
views.note: The same passages from the first page to the last: glimpses in the Old Testament, the Son's coming, his last teaching, and the life of the church.

refs.label: “He will glorify Me”
refs.note: The Spirit takes what is the Son's and makes it known; “Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine.”

refs.label: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son”
refs.note: Jesus prays: “that Your Son may glorify You … glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Eternal life is to know “the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.”

refs.label: “As You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You”
refs.note: He prays that his people may be one as they are one, and share the love the Father had for him “before the foundation of the world.”

groups.title: The cross, the resurrection, and Pentecost
groups.note: The Son offers himself through the Spirit, is raised, sends the disciples as the Father sent him, and pours out the Spirit from the Father.

refs.label: “Not as I will, but as You will”
refs.note: In Gethsemane the Son asks, and yields.

refs.label: “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit”
refs.note: His last words from the cross are a prayer to the Father.

refs.label: “Through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God”
refs.note: The cross itself: the Son offers himself to the Father through the Spirit.

refs.label: “Through the Spirit of holiness … declared with power to be the Son of God”
refs.note: By his resurrection from the dead.

refs.label: “Put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit”
“My Father and your Father, My God and your God”
refs.note: Risen, Jesus calls the disciples his brothers and shares his Father with them.

refs.label: “As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you”
refs.note: Then he breathed on them: “Receive the Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “My Lord and my God!”
refs.note: Thomas, touching the wounds; Jesus accepts the worship.

refs.label: “In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: One name, three persons. The Didache, one of the earliest Christian writings outside the Bible, baptizes in the same words.

refs.label: “Wait for the gift the Father promised”
refs.note: The Son tells them to wait for the Father's promise: baptism with the Holy Spirit.

refs.label: Raised, exalted, and pouring out the Spirit
refs.note: “God has raised this Jesus to life … He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.” Pentecost is all three at once.

groups.title: What the apostles said of God
groups.note: Writing to the churches, the apostles call the Son God, call the Spirit God, and still confess one God.

refs.label: “You have not lied to men, but to God!”
refs.note: Peter says Ananias lied “to the Holy Spirit,” then that he lied to God.

refs.label: “The Holy Spirit said, ‘Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul’”
refs.note: The Spirit speaks, and calls people to himself.

refs.label: One God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ
refs.note: “There is no God but one.” Then Paul splits the Shema's two words between them: “one God, the Father, from whom all things came … one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came.”

refs.label: The Spirit searches the deep things of God
refs.note: “No one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.” We have received “the Spirit who is from God.”

refs.label: “You yourselves are God's temple”
refs.note: The temple is God's because “God's Spirit dwells in you.”

refs.label: “Now the Lord is the Spirit”
refs.note: “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”

refs.label: “Christ, who is God over all”
refs.note: “Forever worthy of praise! Amen.”

refs.label: “All the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form”
One God, and one mediator
refs.note: “There is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

refs.label: “Our great God and Savior Jesus Christ”
“Your throne, O God, endures forever”
refs.note: The Father speaks to the Son and calls him God, then says “God, Your God, has anointed You.”

refs.label: “The Father of the heavenly lights”
refs.note: Every good and perfect gift comes down from him, “with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.”

groups.title: God at work in us
groups.note: Salvation, adoption and prayer are the work of all three: chosen by the Father, redeemed by the Son, sealed and moved by the Spirit.

refs.label: The Spirit of God, the Spirit of Christ
refs.note: One Spirit called by both names; the Spirit of him who raised Jesus will give life to our mortal bodies.

refs.label: “By whom we cry, ‘Abba! Father!’”
refs.note: The Spirit of adoption makes us God's children and co-heirs with Christ.

refs.label: The Spirit intercedes “according to the will of God”
refs.note: He prays for us “with groans too deep for words,” and the Father who searches hearts “knows the mind of the Spirit.”

refs.label: “He who did not spare His own Son”
refs.note: “But gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?”

refs.label: God sent His Son, and the Spirit of His Son
refs.note: “God sent His Son … God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, ‘Abba, Father!’”

refs.label: Chosen, redeemed, sealed
refs.note: The Father chose us “before the foundation of the world,” in the Son “we have redemption through His blood,” and we were “sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “Access to the Father by one Spirit”
refs.note: “Through Him,” the Son. Christian prayer runs through all three.

refs.label: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God”
refs.note: The seal on every believer until the day of redemption.

refs.label: Loved by the Lord, chosen by God, sanctified by the Spirit
“Renewal by the Holy Spirit … poured out on us through Jesus Christ”
refs.note: God our Savior saved us, the Spirit renews us, and the Son is the one through whom the Spirit is poured out.

refs.label: Chosen by the Father, sanctified by the Spirit, for Jesus Christ
refs.note: “According to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ.”

refs.label: “An advocate before the Father”
refs.note: The risen Son speaks to the Father for us. “Advocate” is the word Jesus used when he promised the Spirit as “another Advocate.”

refs.label: “He has given us of His Spirit”
refs.note: “And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent His Son to be the Savior of the world.”

refs.label: Praying in the Spirit, kept in God's love, awaiting Christ's mercy

groups.title: The church's worship, and the end
groups.note: The church's gifts, its unity and its blessing are all three-fold, and at the end the Son hands the kingdom to the Father.

refs.label: “No one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except by the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Every true confession of the Son is the Spirit's work.

refs.label: The same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God
refs.note: Gifts, ministries and ways of working, each traced to one of the three.

refs.label: “As He determines”
refs.note: The Spirit gives each believer gifts by his own will.

refs.label: One Spirit, one Lord, one God and Father of all
The grace, the love, and the fellowship
refs.note: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.”

refs.label: He hands over the kingdom to God the Father
refs.note: At the end the Son hands the kingdom to the Father, “so that God may be all in all.”

views.title: What they do
views.note: Every passage by the verbs of the relationships: who sends, gives, loves, glorifies, prays.

refs.label: “When You send Your Spirit, they are created”

refs.note: A speaker sent by the Lord GOD, with his Spirit.

refs.note: The Spirit, the LORD who anoints, and the one anointed: the scroll Jesus read in Nazareth.

refs.note: A new heart, and God's own Spirit moving his people to walk in his ways.

refs.note: He is given dominion, glory and a kingdom that will never be destroyed. At his trial Jesus took this vision for himself.

refs.label: “I will pour out My Spirit on all people”

refs.note: John the Baptist is told that the one on whom the Spirit rests “is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son”
refs.note: The Father's love for the world is measured by what the Son is to him.

refs.label: “God gives the Spirit without limit”
refs.note: The one God sent speaks God's words, “for God gives the Spirit without limit. The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.”

refs.note: The Son does only what he sees the Father doing; the Father has given him all judgment and “granted the Son to have life in Himself,” so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.

refs.label: “Not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me”
Streams of living water
refs.note: “He was speaking about the Spirit … the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.”

refs.note: The Son asks, the Father gives, the Spirit comes “in My name” to teach. “My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.”

refs.note: The Son sends the Spirit “from the Father,” and the Spirit testifies about the Son. The Nicene Creed takes “proceeds from the Father” from this verse; Western churches later added “and the Son,” a difference still discussed between East and West.

refs.note: The Son's going away is for their good: then he sends the Advocate, who convicts the world.

refs.note: Jesus prays: “that Your Son may glorify You … glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Eternal life is to know “the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.”

refs.note: Then he breathed on them: “Receive the Holy Spirit.”

refs.note: The Son tells them to wait for the Father's promise: baptism with the Holy Spirit.

refs.note: “God has raised this Jesus to life … He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.” Pentecost is all three at once.

refs.note: “But gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?”

refs.note: At the end the Son hands the kingdom to the Father, “so that God may be all in all.”

refs.note: “God sent His Son … God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, ‘Abba, Father!’”

refs.note: The Father chose us “before the foundation of the world,” in the Son “we have redemption through His blood,” and we were “sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “Renewal by the Holy Spirit … poured out on us through Jesus Christ”
refs.note: God our Savior saved us, the Spirit renews us, and the Son is the one through whom the Spirit is poured out.

refs.label: “The exact representation of His nature”
refs.note: God has spoken by his Son, “through whom He made the universe”; the Son is “the radiance of God's glory.”

refs.label: “Through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God”
refs.note: The cross itself: the Son offers himself to the Father through the Spirit.

refs.label: “The Father of the heavenly lights”
refs.note: Every good and perfect gift comes down from him, “with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.”

refs.label: “God sent His one and only Son into the world”
refs.note: “Not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.”

refs.label: “He has given us of His Spirit”
refs.note: “And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent His Son to be the Savior of the world.”

refs.label: “The LORD said to my Lord”
refs.note: Jesus asked how David, speaking “in the Spirit,” could call his own descendant Lord: the LORD, David's Lord, and the Spirit in one verse.

refs.label: “On Him God the Father has placed His seal”

refs.note: Christians have read this of the Son as sent and made man, since the same Gospel opens by calling him God (1:1), and near its end Thomas calls him “My Lord and my God” (20:28).

refs.note: He prays that his people may be one as they are one, and share the love the Father had for him “before the foundation of the world.”

refs.label: “If I drive out demons by the Spirit of God”
refs.note: “Then the kingdom of God has come upon you.” The Son's works are done in the Spirit's power.

refs.label: Blasphemy against the Spirit
refs.note: Jesus speaks of sinning against the Spirit as worse than speaking against the Son of Man.

refs.label: “Not as I will, but as You will”
refs.note: In Gethsemane the Son asks, and yields.

refs.label: “In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: One name, three persons. The Didache, one of the earliest Christian writings outside the Bible, baptizes in the same words.

refs.label: Jesus: “the Lord is One”
refs.note: Asked for the greatest commandment, Jesus answers with the Shema.

refs.label: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me”
refs.note: In Nazareth Jesus reads Isaiah 61 and says “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

refs.label: “Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Rejoicing in the Spirit, the Son praises the Father: “All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son.”

refs.label: “How much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: “To those who ask Him!”

refs.label: “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit”
refs.note: His last words from the cross are a prayer to the Father.

refs.label: “God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son”
refs.note: The Father's love for the world is measured by what the Son is to him.

refs.label: “The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does”
refs.note: The Son does only what he sees the Father doing; the Father has given him all judgment and “granted the Son to have life in Himself,” so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.

refs.label: “On Him God the Father has placed His seal”
refs.note: The Father sets his seal of approval on the Son of Man.

refs.label: “Not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me”
Streams of living water
refs.note: “He was speaking about the Spirit … the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.”

refs.label: “Before Abraham was born, I am!”
refs.note: Echoing the name God gave Moses at the burning bush (Exodus 3:14). His hearers picked up stones.

refs.label: “I and the Father are one”
refs.note: One, yet “I and the Father,” two. They answer: “You, who are a man, make Yourself out to be God.”

refs.label: “Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father”
refs.note: “No one comes to the Father except through Me … I am in the Father and the Father is in Me.”

refs.label: “I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate”
refs.note: The Son asks, the Father gives, the Spirit comes “in My name” to teach. “My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.”

refs.label: “The Father is greater than I”
refs.note: Christians have read this of the Son as sent and made man, since the same Gospel opens by calling him God (1:1), and near its end Thomas calls him “My Lord and my God” (20:28).

refs.label: “I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me … I love the Father”
refs.note: The only place Jesus says in so many words that he loves the Father.

refs.label: “The Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father”
refs.note: The Son sends the Spirit “from the Father,” and the Spirit testifies about the Son. The Nicene Creed takes “proceeds from the Father” from this verse; Western churches later added “and the Son,” a difference still discussed between East and West.

refs.label: “If I go, I will send Him to you”
refs.note: The Son's going away is for their good: then he sends the Advocate, who convicts the world.

refs.label: “He will glorify Me”
refs.note: The Spirit takes what is the Son's and makes it known; “Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine.”

refs.label: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son”
refs.note: Jesus prays: “that Your Son may glorify You … glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” Eternal life is to know “the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.”

refs.label: “As You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You”
refs.note: He prays that his people may be one as they are one, and share the love the Father had for him “before the foundation of the world.”

refs.label: “My Father and your Father, My God and your God”
refs.note: Risen, Jesus calls the disciples his brothers and shares his Father with them.

refs.label: “As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you”
refs.note: Then he breathed on them: “Receive the Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “Wait for the gift the Father promised”
refs.note: The Son tells them to wait for the Father's promise: baptism with the Holy Spirit.

refs.label: “The Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters”
refs.note: At creation, before God speaks.

refs.label: “Let Us make man in Our image”
refs.note: God speaks in the plural, then creates man “in His own image” in the singular. Early Christians heard in the “Us” a first hint of more than one person in the one God.

refs.label: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father”
refs.note: The LORD speaks to his anointed king. The apostles heard the Father speaking to Jesus.

refs.label: “When You send Your Spirit, they are created”
“Where can I go to escape Your Spirit?”
refs.note: The Spirit is as present everywhere as God himself.

refs.label: “Holy, holy, holy”: whose glory, and whose voice?
refs.note: Isaiah sees the Lord, the seraphim cry “holy” three times, and God asks “Who will go for Us?” John says Isaiah saw Jesus' glory; Paul says the Holy Spirit spoke these words.

links.label: Acts 28:25–26
links.topic: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke”

refs.label: “Mighty God”
refs.note: The child born to us will be called “Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.”

links.label: Luke 1:32–33
links.topic: The throne of his father David

refs.label: “I am the LORD, and there is no other”
refs.note: “There is no God but Me.”

refs.label: “The Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit”
refs.note: A speaker sent by the Lord GOD, with his Spirit.

refs.label: “They rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Even here the Spirit is someone who can be grieved. The passage names the LORD, “the Angel of His Presence,” and “His Holy Spirit” together.

links.label: Ephesians 4:30
links.topic: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God”

refs.label: “I will put My Spirit within you”
refs.note: A new heart, and God's own Spirit moving his people to walk in his ways.

refs.label: “I will pour out My Spirit on all people”

links.label: Acts 2:16–18
links.topic: Peter: this is what Joel spoke of

refs.label: “Do we not all have one Father?”
refs.note: “Did not one God create us?” Already in the prophets God is Father to his people.

refs.label: The baptism of Jesus
refs.note: The Son comes up out of the water, the Spirit descends like a dove and rests on him, and the Father's voice says “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”

refs.label: “This is My beloved Son … Listen to Him!”
refs.note: The Father's voice again, on the mountain of transfiguration.

refs.label: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you”
refs.note: “And the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God.”

refs.label: Full of the Spirit, led by the Spirit
refs.note: Into the wilderness to be tempted, then back to Galilee “in the power of the Spirit.”

refs.label: “The Word was with God, and the Word was God”
refs.note: With God, so distinct from the Father; God, so not less than him. “Through Him all things were made.”

refs.label: “The Word became flesh”
refs.note: “We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father.”

refs.label: “The one and only Son, who is Himself God”
refs.note: “No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father's side, has made Him known.”

refs.label: The Spirit descends and rests on Him
refs.note: John the Baptist is told that the one on whom the Spirit rests “is He who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “God gives the Spirit without limit”
refs.note: The one God sent speaks God's words, “for God gives the Spirit without limit. The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in His hands.”

refs.label: “Making Himself equal with God”
refs.note: His opponents understood what calling God “His own Father” meant.

refs.label: “My Lord and my God!”
refs.note: Thomas, touching the wounds; Jesus accepts the worship.

refs.label: Raised, exalted, and pouring out the Spirit
refs.note: “God has raised this Jesus to life … He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit and has poured out what you now see and hear.” Pentecost is all three at once.

refs.label: “You have not lied to men, but to God!”
refs.note: Peter says Ananias lied “to the Holy Spirit,” then that he lied to God.

refs.label: “God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power”
refs.note: Peter's summary of Jesus's whole ministry, “because God was with Him.”

refs.label: “The Holy Spirit said, ‘Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul’”
refs.note: The Spirit speaks, and calls people to himself.

refs.label: “Through the Spirit of holiness … declared with power to be the Son of God”
refs.note: By his resurrection from the dead.

refs.label: The Spirit of God, the Spirit of Christ
refs.note: One Spirit called by both names; the Spirit of him who raised Jesus will give life to our mortal bodies.

refs.label: “By whom we cry, ‘Abba! Father!’”
refs.note: The Spirit of adoption makes us God's children and co-heirs with Christ.

refs.label: The Spirit intercedes “according to the will of God”
refs.note: He prays for us “with groans too deep for words,” and the Father who searches hearts “knows the mind of the Spirit.”

refs.label: “He who did not spare His own Son”
refs.note: “But gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?”

refs.label: “Christ, who is God over all”
refs.note: “Forever worthy of praise! Amen.”

refs.label: The Spirit searches the deep things of God
refs.note: “No one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.” We have received “the Spirit who is from God.”

refs.label: “You yourselves are God's temple”
refs.note: The temple is God's because “God's Spirit dwells in you.”

refs.label: One God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ
refs.note: “There is no God but one.” Then Paul splits the Shema's two words between them: “one God, the Father, from whom all things came … one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came.”

refs.label: “No one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except by the Holy Spirit”
refs.note: Every true confession of the Son is the Spirit's work.

refs.label: The same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God
refs.note: Gifts, ministries and ways of working, each traced to one of the three.

refs.label: “As He determines”
refs.note: The Spirit gives each believer gifts by his own will.

refs.label: He hands over the kingdom to God the Father
refs.note: At the end the Son hands the kingdom to the Father, “so that God may be all in all.”

refs.label: “Now the Lord is the Spirit”
refs.note: “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”

refs.label: The grace, the love, and the fellowship
refs.note: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.”

refs.label: God sent His Son, and the Spirit of His Son
refs.note: “God sent His Son … God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, ‘Abba, Father!’”

refs.label: Chosen, redeemed, sealed
refs.note: The Father chose us “before the foundation of the world,” in the Son “we have redemption through His blood,” and we were “sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.”

refs.label: “Access to the Father by one Spirit”
refs.note: “Through Him,” the Son. Christian prayer runs through all three.

refs.label: One Spirit, one Lord, one God and Father of all
“Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God”
refs.note: The seal on every believer until the day of redemption.

refs.label: In the form of God, obedient to death
refs.note: “Existing in the form of God,” he emptied himself and “became obedient to death.” So the Father exalted him, and every tongue confesses him Lord “to the glory of God the Father.”

refs.label: “The image of the invisible God”
refs.note: “All things were created through Him and for Him … For God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him.”

refs.label: “All the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form”
Loved by the Lord, chosen by God, sanctified by the Spirit
One God, and one mediator
refs.note: “There is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

refs.label: “Our great God and Savior Jesus Christ”
“Renewal by the Holy Spirit … poured out on us through Jesus Christ”
refs.note: God our Savior saved us, the Spirit renews us, and the Son is the one through whom the Spirit is poured out.

refs.label: “The exact representation of His nature”
refs.note: God has spoken by his Son, “through whom He made the universe”; the Son is “the radiance of God's glory.”

refs.label: “Your throne, O God, endures forever”
refs.note: The Father speaks to the Son and calls him God, then says “God, Your God, has anointed You.”

refs.label: “Through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God”
refs.note: The cross itself: the Son offers himself to the Father through the Spirit.

refs.label: “The Father of the heavenly lights”
refs.note: Every good and perfect gift comes down from him, “with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.”

refs.label: Chosen by the Father, sanctified by the Spirit, for Jesus Christ
refs.note: “According to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ.”

refs.label: “Put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit”
“An advocate before the Father”
refs.note: The risen Son speaks to the Father for us. “Advocate” is the word Jesus used when he promised the Spirit as “another Advocate.”

refs.label: “God sent His one and only Son into the world”
refs.note: “Not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.”

refs.label: “He has given us of His Spirit”
refs.note: “And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent His Son to be the Savior of the world.”

refs.label: Praying in the Spirit, kept in God's love, awaiting Christ's mercy
